solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Finish huge company image used in keyhole surgery?

parts.note: to finish is to end
OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize
PIC is short for picture, an image

explanation.surface: A puzzling business slogan about wrapping up a giant firm's picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Keyhole surgery works through a tiny incision with a viewing scope, the adjective for that kind of internal camera work.

clue.text: Wooden items include superior serving bowl

indicators.note: include means the wooden items wrap around the superior letter

parts.note: treen is small household ware made of wood
U is the old British abbreviation for upper-class, superior

explanation.surface: A set of carved woodware that also contains a fine dish for the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep lidded dish from which soup is ladled at table is exactly a serving bowl.

clue.text: Drink one to limit bone disease

indicators.note: to limit something is to hem it in, so the drink encloses the bone

parts.note: beer is a drink
a rib is a bone
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A bar instruction: have a drink, but only one, to stop a bone disease.
explanation.definitionFit: A vitamin B1 deficiency illness is a disease, so the bare word defines it.

clue.text: British officer upended axis

indicators.note: upended in a down clue means the officer is read from bottom to top

parts.note: COL is short for colonel, an army officer

explanation.surface: A British officer turned upside down along some line or pivot.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis in the political sense is an alliance of nations, which is a grouping of allied states.

clue.text: Miss train miles outside Arkansas

parts.note: to school someone is to train them

indicators.note: outside says the miles go around the state's code

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mile, doubled here for the plural
AR is the postal code for Arkansas

explanation.surface: Someone misses a train while miles beyond Arkansas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a verb about failing to catch the train, but it is the title a teacher is addressed by.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils call a female teacher Miss, and a prim old-fashioned teacher is a stock figure.

clue.text: Weightlifters use them to purchase fungi by phone

indicators.note: by phone means the words are judged as heard over a line, by sound only

parts.note: to purchase is to buy; ceps are edible mushrooms, a kind of fungi

explanation.surface: Bodybuilders order wild mushrooms over the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting weights works the upper-arm muscles hardest, so these are what weightlifters use.

clue.text: Pick up Irish porcelain associated with banks

indicators.note: pick up in a down clue lifts the letters so they read upwards

parts.note: Parian is a white unglazed porcelain resembling marble

explanation.surface: Collect some Irish china that has links to the banking world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' suggests finance; here they are the banks of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things living or sited on riverbanks, a technical term for riverside.

clue.text: Behavioural trait expressed by egoist?

definitions.meaning: a unit of cultural behaviour passed from person to person by imitation
a self-centred person keeps saying the first-person pronoun, twice over

explanation.surface: A habit shown by someone who thinks only of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawkins coined the term for a cultural trait spread by copying, the behavioural analogue of a gene.

clue.text: Novel clue (cryptic) I found in Paris factory making fresh food

indicators.note: cryptic means obscured, so the novel and clue letters are jumbled
found in puts the I inside the French word

parts.note: usine is French for factory, French being the language of Paris

explanation.surface: A novel's cryptic clue tracked down in a French factory producing new food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' rearranges the first two words into NOUVELLEC; 'found in' puts I into the French word USINE, giving UISINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The style is literally French for new cooking, lighter dishes made from fresh ingredients.

clue.text: Cross references in Vile Bodies withdrawn

indicators.note: withdrawn says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Mentions of the cross found in Evelyn Waugh's novel Vile Bodies have been removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the letters sit within the title; 'withdrawn' turns ILEBO round.
explanation.definitionFit: Obelus marks are dagger-shaped symbols printed to refer readers to footnotes, so they are cross-shaped references.

clue.text: Our Henry put away work altogether, so I've heard

definitions.note: to work together; 'so I've heard' flags that the two charade words, said as one, give the word

parts.note: Henry Cooper was a much-loved British heavyweight boxer, hence 'our'
to put away food is to eat it, so put away means ate

explanation.surface: Gossip that our Henry has stopped working altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Cooper was a much-loved 1960s British heavyweight boxing champion. 'so I've heard' asks you to say 'Cooper ate' aloud as one word; the spelling is unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: To act jointly towards a common end is to work together.

clue.text: Leave dance for the long haul?

parts.note: congé is permission to depart, leave
a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: Taking time off from dancing to go on a lengthy trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the long haul' sounds like a lengthy journey, but it is a catch hauled from the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A large eel can be well over two metres, so landing it is a lengthy catch for an angler.

clue.text: Track ancient mariners supplying purgative

parts.note: Epsom is an English racecourse, home of the Derby
old salts are veteran sailors

explanation.surface: A racecourse's old sailors handing out a laxative.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnesium sulphate crystals are taken as a laxative, a classic purging remedy.

clue.text: Small lean wader

parts.note: to lean is to tilt

explanation.surface: A slight, thin bird that walks in shallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lean' looks like an adjective (thin) but works as the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged shorebird that feeds in shallow water is a type of wading bird.

clue.text: Penny leaves old money for sort of suite or suit

indicators.note: leaves means the penny goes out of the coin's name

parts.note: a threepenny piece was a pre-decimal British coin

explanation.surface: A penny is dropped from old cash to buy some furniture or clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A threepenny piece (or 'thruppenny bit') was a small British coin before decimalisation in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa with two armchairs, or jacket, trousers and waistcoat, both come as three-item sets.

clue.text: With which writer makes good points?

definitions.text: With which writer makes good points?

parts.words: With which writer makes good points?
parts.note: a writer here is a pencil, and good points are sharp tips rather than sound arguments

explanation.surface: Asking what tool an author uses to argue well.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bladed device that sharpens a pencil gives the writing implement a fine point.

clue.text: English lad, upset, grabs fodder in these

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the letters over so they read upwards

parts.note: a son is a lad
to bag something is to grab it

explanation.surface: An upset English boy snatches animal feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Feed bags hung over a horse's head carry its fodder.

clue.text: Go in through this surgery to save king's rib

indicators.note: to save is to keep safe inside, so these letters hold the king

parts.note: a porch is an entrance one goes in through
K is the abbreviation for king in chess
OP is short for operation, surgery

explanation.surface: A surgeon enters via this route to rescue a king's damaged rib.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of meat on the bone from a pig's ribs is a rib in butchery terms.

clue.text: Damages function way back

parts.note: cos is the cosine, a trigonometric function

indicators.note: back says the street's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Damage done as a road's function is set back.
explanation.definitionFit: Court-ordered sums such as damages and costs are both money a loser pays.

clue.text: US port snarled up, result of too much snow?

indicators.note: snarled up, like jammed traffic, means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An American harbour blocked after a heavy snowfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snow' is slang for cocaine, not weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A dazed state of near-unconsciousness can follow taking too much of a drug.

clue.text: Noteworthy island city motorway, westbound

indicators.note: westbound in an across clue means read right to left

parts.note: Elba is a Mediterranean island
Rome is a city

explanation.surface: A notable trip from an island city heading west on the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth remembering is notable, worth taking note of.

clue.text: You can't miss this bolt

definitions.meaning: said of something unbeatable, a thing you cannot top
to bolt is to run away, scram

explanation.surface: A lock fitting you will not fail to spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'get lost!' as an order to flee and, as 'can't beat it', unmissable.

clue.text: Crush inferior ropemaker, absorbing good one

parts.note: sub means below or inferior

indicators.note: absorbing means the fibre takes the letters inside it

parts.note: jute is fibre used to make rope
A is the indefinite article, one

explanation.surface: Defeat a second-rate rope manufacturer who takes over a good worker.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a people under total control is to crush or subdue them.

clue.text: Second wooden frame

parts.note: ash is a timber, so wooden gives the tree name

explanation.surface: Another wooden structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A window's sliding frame that holds the glass panes is called by this name.

clue.text: Water-carrier, with or without lid

parts.note: a large jug carries water whether or not it has a cover, and a drain that carries water loses its top letter to give the same jug

explanation.surface: A jug that may or may not have a cover.
explanation.walkthrough: A second reading: SEWER is also a water-carrier, and without its lid (first letter) it leaves the jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-mouthed pitcher is a vessel for carrying water.

clue.text: Fleece current American denizen

parts.note: a fleece is a sheep's coat
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An American resident wearing a fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: A raccoon-like mammal native to the Americas lives there, a denizen of that continent.

clue.text: Indicator from old Ford Scorpio maybe

definitions.meaning: the Zodiac was a 1950s-60s Ford saloon, so its badge or signal would be a sign of that car
Scorpio is one of the twelve astrological star signs

explanation.surface: A turn signal taken off a vintage Ford Scorpio car.
explanation.walkthrough: Ford made both a Zodiac and a Scorpio, so the surface stays in the car showroom; here Scorpio is the astrological sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is one of the twelve astrological star signs, an example of the category.
